title.purpose: Panel and section headers (nav section labels, header titles).

body.purpose: Default UI copy, form labels, list content.

label.purpose: Badge counts, timestamps, dense caption text below Tailwind's default text-xs.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Default state for panels, cards, static surfaces (shadow-sm).

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Modals, slide-overs, and other page-overlaying surfaces (shadow-lg).

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Default button treatment — transparent at rest, color appears on hover/focus. Reach for this first for any new action.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--ui-text-muted, #64748b); border: none; border-radius: 0.75rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.875rem; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover, .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ui-primary, #0ea5e9) 10%, transparent); color: var(--ui-primary, #0ea5e9); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ui-primary, #0ea5e9); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid, high-emphasis action. Reserved for the single most important action on a screen — not a default.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--ui-primary, #0ea5e9); color: #ffffff; border: none; border-radius: 0.75rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease, transform 0.1s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ui-primary, #0ea5e9) 85%, black); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ui-primary, #0ea5e9); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The general panel/container primitive (58 uses across v8). Flat by default; resting shadow only.
components.html:
Album statistics

1,204 photos across 38 albums.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--ui-bg-elevated, #ffffff); border: 1px solid var(--ui-border-default, #e2e8f0); border-radius: 0.5rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.05); padding: 1rem; } .ds-card-title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.125rem; line-height: 1.4; margin: 0 0 0.5rem; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--ui-text-muted, #64748b); margin: 0; }

components.name: Photo Tile
components.description: Signature elevated surface. Permanent Raised shadow with a black tint (not gray) to tie it to the darkroom photo-chrome mood; rounds by default (user-configurable off).
components.css: .ds-photo-tile { display: block; position: relative; border-radius: 0.5rem; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); transition: transform 0.2s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-photo-tile:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-photo-tile-img { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; }

components.name: Album Tile (fan hover)
components.description: The system's signature gesture: three stacked copies of the cover image; on hover the back two fan out with a small rotate + translate, reading as a hand-spread stack of prints. Keep unique to albums — the meaning depends on scarcity.
components.css: .ds-album-tile { position: relative; display: block; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; cursor: pointer; } .ds-album-tile-layer { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 0.5rem; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); transition: transform 0.2s ease-out; } .ds-album-tile-layer img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; display: block; } .ds-album-tile:hover .ds-album-tile-layer--back-a { transform: rotate(-2deg) translate(-0.75rem, 0.5rem); } .ds-album-tile:hover .ds-album-tile-layer--back-b { transform: rotate(6deg) translate(0.75rem, -0.5rem); }

components.name: Role Badge
components.description: Corner flag badge on album/photo tiles. Icon-only, colored via the closed flag-hue role map — never a raw hex at the call site.
components.css: .ds-badge-flag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 1.25rem; height: 1.25rem; border-radius: 9999px; color: #ffffff; } .ds-badge-flag--nsfw { background: #d946ef; } .ds-badge-flag--trophy { background: #06b6d4; } .ds-badge-flag--person { background: #9333ea; } .ds-badge-flag--rated { background: #f97316; }

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: Vertical nav item inside the off-canvas slide-over. Small leading icon, muted at rest, primary on hover/active.
components.html: Albums128
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.625rem; border-radius: 0.375rem; color: var(--ui-text-muted, #64748b); font-size: 1rem; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease; } .ds-nav-item:hover, .ds-nav-item--active { color: var(--ui-primary, #0ea5e9); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ui-primary, #0ea5e9) 8%, transparent); } .ds-nav-item-icon { width: 0.75rem; height: 0.75rem; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-nav-item-count { margin-left: auto; background: var(--ui-primary, #0ea5e9); color: #ffffff; font-size: 0.65rem; line-height: 0.8rem; padding: 0.0625rem 0.375rem; border-radius: 9999px; }

narrative.overview:
Lychee v8 is the panel around the photograph, not a rival to it. The chrome is calm and restrained — neutral slate/zinc surfaces, ghost-first buttons, sky blue spent sparingly — so that when a photo appears, it's the only saturated thing on screen. That restraint is deliberate console-craft, not blankness: the interface is precise and utilitarian where it's doing archive work (dense lists, bulk-edit tables, sticky headers, badges that pack a lot of state into a few pixels), and warmer and more tactile exactly where the user is handling photos directly — album tiles fan out into a small stack of offset prints on hover, tiles pick up a soft shadow when they become interactive, corners round off.

The "darkroom" isn't a literal dark theme; it's the photo-viewing chrome specifically: the lightbox goes to true black, tile shadows lean into shadow-black/25 rather than a generic gray, and NSFW/face overlays behave like something you'd handle carefully under red light. Everywhere that isn't directly framing a photo — nav, forms, tables, settings — stays on the ordinary slate/zinc console surface. This is the load-bearing distinction: darkroom mood belongs to the photo-viewing surfaces, not the whole app.

This is a self-hosted tool competing on native-app-feel and simplicity against heavier all-in-one platforms; the UI earns that by never reading as a generic open-source admin panel — no boxy unstyled tables, no default-Bootstrap chrome, no dashboard sprawl for its own sake.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral-first surfaces (slate light / zinc dark); sky blue is a rare accent, not a wash.
Ghost/soft buttons dominate; solid fills are reserved for the one action that matters on a screen.
Photos and their framing (tiles, lightbox, overlays) are the only place true black and visible shadow live.
A small, named palette of "flag" hues (fuchsia, cyan, purple, orange) carries semantic badge meaning and appears nowhere else.
Dialogs and slide-over drawers, not push-down panels — content position never jumps when a tool opens.

rules.name: The One Role, One Hue Rule
rules.body: Every badge role maps to exactly one hue at exactly one light/dark shade pair, centralized in albumBadgeColors.ts. A new badge role gets a new named entry there — never a hardcoded bg-[#hex] or a borrowed Tailwind shade at the call site.

rules.name: The Chrome Stays Neutral Rule
rules.body: Sky blue and the semantic colors are the only colors permitted on ordinary UI chrome. If a screen needs more than one accent hue outside the flag-badge context, that's a sign color is being used decoratively, not semantically.

rules.name: The No Display Face Rule
rules.body: v8 loads no separate display/hero typeface. Every future component reuses the system body stack; introducing a second font family is a departure-mode decision, not a component-level one.

rules.name: The Photos Get Weight Rule
rules.body: Visible shadow is earned by being a photograph or something that floats above the page (modal/drawer). Ordinary chrome stays flat; depth is not spent on furniture.

rules.name: The Ghost-First Rule
rules.body: Every new button starts as ghost. Escalate to soft, then outline, then — only when a screen has exactly one action that must win — solid.

dos: Do default every new button to ghost, escalating through soft/outline before ever reaching solid.
Do author badge and flag colors through the AlbumBadgeRole map, never a call-site hex or ad hoc Tailwind shade.
Do use Nuxt UI's semantic scale (text-muted/text-toned/text-highlighted, bg-default/bg-elevated/bg-muted, border-default/border-muted/border-accented) for anything that must adapt across light/dark.
Do keep the Raised shadow (shadow-md shadow-black/25) exclusive to photo/album tiles.
Do reach for a dialog or slide-over for any bulk tool, filter panel, or settings surface.
donts: Don't use the PrimeUI-era utility classes text-muted-color, text-muted-color-emphasis, or text-primary-emphasis in v8 — they resolve to nothing.
Don't hardcode a raw hex or an off-map Tailwind shade for anything that already has a semantic or role-based token available.
Don't spend a flag-palette hue outside the album/photo badge context.
Don't reach for bg-black/text-white directly for new chrome, except within the lightbox/overlay photo-viewing chrome where true black is the intended darkroom treatment.
Don't let the interface read as a generic self-hosted admin panel.
